'''Decipher WARS Radio''' ('''WARS Radio''') was Decipher's weekly audio show for the [[WARS TCG]], 25 June 2004 – 21 January 2005, 24 episodes. It replaced [[Radio Free Decipher]] and was hosted by [[Mark Tuttle]], Decipher's PR and Marketing Manager.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher], LOTR-TCG Player's Council wiki (sections "Decipher WARS Radio" and "Decipher Games Radio": dates, lengths, episode descriptions, missing files).</ref>

== History ==

[[Radio Free Decipher]] ended with Broadcast 196 on 30 April 2004, in which [[Tim Ellington]] discussed the newly announced WARS TCG.<ref name="yt-5K5m0Yywu_Q">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5K5m0Yywu_Q Broadcast 196 - Radio Free Decipher (30 April, 2004): Tim Ellington on WARS TCG], Player's Council (15 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-5K5m0Yywu_Q Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher then moved the show's resources to a podcast devoted to WARS alone, distributed as MP3 files instead of RealAudio.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher], LOTR-TCG Player's Council wiki (sections "Decipher WARS Radio" and "Decipher Games Radio": dates, lengths, episode descriptions, missing files).</ref><ref name="warsfanhq">[http://web.archive.org/web/20050207162310/http://warstcg.fanhq.com/Articles/Article.aspx?ID=329 Decipher WARS Radio archive], warstcg.fanhq.com. Preserved copy: [http://web.archive.org/web/20050207162310/http://warstcg.fanhq.com/Articles/Article.aspx?ID=329 Internet Archive].</ref> Regular segments included listener email, a weekly "Big Reveal" of WARS art or cards, and interviews with Decipher Games Studio staff.

WARS TCG used a game engine derived from the Star Wars CCG. Episode 8 (13 August 2004) presented WARS as "the game that's bringing back the SWCCG mechanics".<ref name="yt-o5tIK-kooDA">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o5tIK-kooDA Ep. 8 - Decipher WARS Radio (13 August, 2004): Gen Con Indy and First Tournament Weekend Gen Con], Player's Council (15 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-o5tIK-kooDA Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="lotrpc-rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher], LOTR-TCG Player's Council wiki (sections "Decipher WARS Radio" and "Decipher Games Radio": dates, lengths, episode descriptions, missing files).</ref>

=== Warren Holland interviews ===

Decipher Chairman and CEO [[Warren Holland]] appears in three episodes:
* Episode 3 (9 July 2004): the first part of an interview on the roots of the WARS TCG project.<ref name="yt-lxL-5bskkaw">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lxL-5bskkaw Ep. 3 - Decipher WARS Radio (09 July, 2004): Warren Holland Interview; What's Happening in Art], Player's Council (15 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-lxL-5bskkaw Internet Archive].</ref>
* Episode 4 (16 July 2004): the second part of the interview.<ref name="yt-FWBYRjMvhZw">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FWBYRjMvhZw Ep. 4 - Decipher WARS Radio (16 July, 2004): Holland Interview Part 2 and a Gongen Big Reveal!], Player's Council (15 May 2022).</ref>
* Episode 16 (6 October 2004): opening a pack on WARS release week and discussing the previous seven months of work.<ref name="yt-liVMsN5d5sE">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=liVMsN5d5sE Ep. 16 - Decipher WARS Radio (06 October, 2004): Crack a Pack], Player's Council (15 May 2022). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-liVMsN5d5sE Internet Archive].</ref>

After WARS Radio, Decipher ran a short successor, [[Decipher Games Radio]] (March–April 2005).

== Episodes ==

Episode 20 (3 December 2004) is not among the recovered files.<ref name="lotrpc-rfd">[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Radio_Free_Decipher Radio Free Decipher], LOTR-TCG Player's Council wiki (sections "Decipher WARS Radio" and "Decipher Games Radio": dates, lengths, episode descriptions, missing files).</ref>
